newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Donetsk takes lead in World Cities Chess.
newsitem.headline: Donetsk takes lead in World Cities Chess.

text.p: The Ukrainian team Donetsk took a clear lead at the half-way point in the inaugural World Cities Chess Championship by outclassing the previous tournament leader Oslo on Thursday in Jakarta.

The all-Grandmaster Donetsk team defeated the Norwegians by a comfortable 3-1 margin and would have done even better had not Stanislav Savchenko allowed his opponent Jonathan Tisdall to escape with a remarkable draw in a desperate rook and pawn endgame.
With only a few minutes remaining in the four hour playing session, Savchenko missed the opportunity to play a simple winning move, noticed by all the spectators but not by either player.
"I can't believe he missed that!" exclaimed Tisdall's teammate Einar Gausel after Savchenko had let the win slip. "It's nice to see that even an endgame expert can screw up sometimes," Gausel added.
"What can you do?" said a relieved Tisdall after the game. "I just had to struggle on. At least that makes up for my miss in this morning's game."
Donetsk's nearest rivals are the top seeded Moscow who enjoyed a similar 3-1 winning margin over Bandung.
The Russians missed out on a clean sweep and the outright tournament lead when Alexander Onischuk was tricked by low rated Salor Sitanggang.

"I blundered - it was horrible," said Onischuk, who has yet to win a ame, after his defeat. "I am playing very badly," admitted the world-class Grandmaster. Donetsk and Moscow will meet in the sixth round on Friday in a match-up which is likely to decide the tournament victor. The World Cities Championship concludes on July 14.
